headline: High: caveman can feed untrusted content into Chatwoot workflows, creating prompt-injection and cascading-action risk; data leakage is limited by caveman’s no-egress profile.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: caveman uses MCP and file surfaces like CLAUDE.md/project notes, while Chatwoot exposes integrations and broad network egress. A shared workspace or copied content could let attacker-controlled text from Chatwoot reach caveman as trusted instructions. The pairwise pathway is plausible but not directly documented, so uncertainty pushes to medium.
conditions: IF Chatwoot content is copied into caveman-readable files or MCP inputs
IF caveman treats imported file content as instructions rather than data
mitigations: Restrict caveman to a dedicated workspace
Disable or gate MCP ingestion for Chatwoot-derived text
Add a manual review step before writing Chatwoot content into CLAUDE.md or notes
Use provenance tags on imported snippets
requires-engineering: enforce content-type separation between instructions and customer text

B_data_leakage.rationale: caveman lists no network egress, so it is unlikely to exfiltrate data by itself, while Chatwoot handles customer data and can call external integrations. The pair can still expose customer text if shared files or copied notes move between them, but the blast radius is limited by caveman’s local-only posture and the lack of a documented shared workspace.
conditions: IF customer data from Chatwoot is placed into caveman files or prompts
IF Chatwoot integrations export that same data to third parties
mitigations: Keep customer records out of caveman project files
Use redacted excerpts when drafting with caveman
Review Chatwoot integration destinations before enabling them
Separate support and writing workspaces
requires-engineering: add DLP checks on shared files

C_capability_conflict.rationale: caveman supports multiple instances and writes project files, while Chatwoot has broad network egress and integration surfaces. The profiles do not show overlapping write access to the same mutable resource, so a direct conflict is not established. Uncertainty remains because shared filesystem or OAuth scopes are not documented, so low is the safest supported level.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same writable directory
IF Chatwoot integrations and caveman edits target the same external resource
mitigations: Assign separate directories per agent
Avoid concurrent edits to shared files
Disable unused Chatwoot integrations
Stagger runs when both touch the same project
requires-engineering: add locking around shared mutable resources

D_cascading_error.rationale: caveman produces project notes and CLAUDE.md content that Chatwoot could ingest if operators reuse text across workflows. Chatwoot’s support tooling and integrations can then act on that content, so A’s output may become B’s input without a verification gate. The interaction is inferred rather than documented, so medium fits the default-risk pathway.
conditions: IF caveman-generated text is pasted into Chatwoot macros, replies, or reports
IF Chatwoot actions are triggered from unverified caveman output
mitigations: Require human review before reusing caveman output in Chatwoot
Mark caveman drafts as non-authoritative
Use templates that separate facts from recommendations
Audit Chatwoot automations that consume pasted text
requires-engineering: add verification metadata between agents

E_compliance.rationale: caveman touches session logs, memory files, and project notes, while Chatwoot touches customer data, contact profiles, and interaction history. If the pair is used on the same regulated customer content, retention or residency mismatches can arise. The profiles do not specify certifications or residency, so the compliance risk is inferred and medium rather than high.
conditions: IF regulated customer data is copied into caveman logs or notes
IF Chatwoot retention settings differ from caveman file retention
mitigations: Avoid placing regulated data in caveman notes
Set explicit retention rules for shared artifacts
Review Chatwoot data export and deletion settings
Use pseudonymized examples in drafts
requires-engineering: align retention and residency policies
